name: RESTful API Security
description: Threat model for a RESTful API service with OAuth2 authentication, handling sensitive customer data and financial transactions.

components.name: API Gateway
components.description: Entry point for all API requests, handles routing, rate limiting, and basic validation

components.name: OAuth2 Auth Service
components.description: Issues and validates JWT tokens, manages API keys and client credentials

components.name: Business Logic Service
components.description: Core API endpoints for customer data and transaction processing

components.name: PostgreSQL Database
components.description: Stores customer profiles, transaction history, and API audit logs

components.name: Redis Cache
components.description: Caches JWT tokens, rate limit counters, and frequently accessed data

components.name: Third-Party API Clients
components.description: Mobile apps, web applications, and partner integrations consuming the API

components.name: Payment Gateway
components.description: External payment processor for financial transactions

dataFlows.data: Customer data queries and transaction records
Payment processing requests with PCI data

trustBoundaries.name: Internet Boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Separates external clients from internal API infrastructure

trustBoundaries.name: Internal Services Boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Separates API services from data stores and external payment systems

threats.title: JWT Token Forgery
threats.description: Attacker attempts to forge JWT tokens using weak signing algorithms (e.g., 'none' algorithm) or stolen signing keys to impersonate legitimate users.

threats.title: API Key Theft and Reuse
threats.description: API keys stored insecurely in mobile apps or client-side code can be extracted and reused by unauthorized parties.

threats.title: API Request Manipulation
threats.description: Attacker modifies request parameters (e.g., user_id, amount) to access other users' data or manipulate transaction amounts.

threats.title: Mass Assignment Vulnerability
threats.description: API endpoints accept more input fields than intended, allowing attackers to modify protected fields like 'isAdmin' or 'balance'.

threats.title: Insufficient API Audit Logging
threats.description: API requests, especially sensitive operations like data exports or financial transactions, lack comprehensive logging, making incident investigation difficult.

threats.title: Excessive Data Exposure
threats.description: API responses return complete database objects with sensitive fields (e.g., password hashes, SSN, internal IDs) instead of filtered views.

threats.title: Verbose Error Messages
threats.description: API returns detailed error messages including stack traces, database queries, and internal paths, revealing system architecture to attackers.

threats.title: GraphQL Query Introspection in Production
threats.description: If using GraphQL, introspection queries reveal entire API schema including internal fields and relationships to potential attackers.

threats.title: Lack of Rate Limiting
threats.description: API endpoints lack rate limiting, allowing attackers to flood the service with requests, causing service degradation or complete outage.

threats.title: Resource Exhaustion via Pagination
threats.description: API pagination parameters (e.g., ?limit=999999) allow requesting massive datasets, exhausting memory and database resources.

threats.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
threats.description: API endpoints fail to verify that the authenticated user has permission to access the requested resource ID (e.g., GET /api/users/123).

threats.title: Broken Function Level Authorization
threats.description: Regular users can access admin endpoints (e.g., DELETE /api/users) because authorization checks only verify authentication, not role permissions.

mitigations.title: Enforce Strong JWT Algorithms
mitigations.description: Use RS256 or ES256 (asymmetric) algorithms. Explicitly reject 'none' algorithm. Rotate signing keys regularly. Store private keys in HSM or secure vault.
mitigations.implementation: Configure JWT library to only accept RS256/ES256. Implement key rotation every 90 days.

mitigations.title: Implement Token Expiration and Refresh
mitigations.description: Issue short-lived access tokens (15 minutes) with longer-lived refresh tokens. Implement token revocation list.
mitigations.implementation: Set JWT exp claim to 15 minutes. Use Redis to track revoked tokens.

mitigations.title: Implement API Key Rotation and Scoping
mitigations.description: Require regular API key rotation. Scope keys to specific permissions and IP ranges. Use short-lived keys for mobile apps.
mitigations.implementation: Force 90-day key rotation. Implement OAuth2 PKCE for mobile apps instead of static keys.

mitigations.title: Implement Object-Level Authorization
mitigations.description: Always verify that the authenticated user owns or has permission to access the requested resource ID before returning data.

mitigations.title: Use Allowlists for Input Fields
mitigations.description: Explicitly define which fields can be set by users. Reject any unexpected fields. Use DTOs/schemas to validate input.
mitigations.implementation: Use Zod or class-validator to define allowed fields. Strip unknown properties.

mitigations.title: Comprehensive API Audit Logging
mitigations.description: Log all API requests with timestamp, user ID, IP, endpoint, method, response code, and sensitive operation details.
mitigations.implementation: Use structured logging (JSON). Send logs to SIEM. Retain for 90+ days.

mitigations.title: Implement Response Filtering
mitigations.description: Create DTOs/view models that only include necessary fields. Never return complete database objects directly.
mitigations.implementation: Use GraphQL field resolvers or REST serializers to filter responses.

mitigations.title: Generic Error Responses in Production
mitigations.description: Return generic error messages to clients. Log detailed errors server-side only.
mitigations.implementation: Production: 'An error occurred'. Logs: Full stack trace.

mitigations.title: Disable GraphQL Introspection in Production
mitigations.description: Disable introspection queries in production environments. Provide schema documentation via separate secure channel.
mitigations.implementation: Set introspection: false in Apollo Server config for production.

mitigations.title: Implement Multi-Layer Rate Limiting
mitigations.description: Apply rate limits at multiple levels: per IP, per API key, per endpoint. Use sliding window algorithm.
mitigations.implementation: Use Redis-backed rate limiting. 100 req/min per IP, 1000/min per API key.

mitigations.title: Enforce Pagination Limits
mitigations.description: Set hard maximum limits for pagination (e.g., max 100 items per page). Implement cursor-based pagination for large datasets.
mitigations.implementation: Enforce max limit=100. Use cursor pagination for lists > 1000 items.

mitigations.title: Object-Level Authorization Framework
mitigations.description: Implement framework that automatically checks resource ownership. Use policy-based access control (e.g., Casbin, OPA).
mitigations.implementation: Create middleware that verifies user owns resource before any operation.

mitigations.title: Function-Level Authorization Checks
mitigations.description: Implement role-based or permission-based checks on all endpoints. Deny by default, allow by exception.
